_doc: Curated demo Cypher queries for the Neo4j Browser, run against the MS GraphRAG knowledge graph loaded by `ke neo4j load` (schema: (:Entity)-[:RELATED_TO]->(:Entity), (:Entity)-[:IN_COMMUNITY]->(:Community), (:Community)-[:PARENT_OF]->(:Community), (:Entity)-[:MENTIONED_IN]->(:TextUnit)). Entity titles are UPPER-CASED as emitted by GraphRAG. These mirror the chat demo ladder — especially the Character.AI relationship-bridging case that BM25 cannot answer — so the graph view can be shown side-by-side with the agent answer. The webui right column renders each as a copyable code block plus a deep link into http://localhost:7474/browser/.
auth_hint: default auth: neo4j / graphrag-demo (override with NEO4J_PASSWORD)

queries.label: Graph at a glance
queries.description: Node counts per label — entities, communities, text units.
queries.cypher: MATCH (n) RETURN labels(n)[0] AS label, count(*) AS count ORDER BY count DESC;

queries.label: Schema (labels + relationships)
queries.description: Visual meta-graph of node labels and relationship types.

queries.label: ⭐ Character.AI incident graph
queries.description: 1-hop neighbourhood of CHARACTER.AI. This is the relationship-bridging case BM25 fails on: the victims (Sewell Setzer, Jennifer Ann Crecente), the lawsuit, and the Google deal all surface as connected entities.

queries.label: Character.AI — 2-hop context
queries.description: Expand two hops out from CHARACTER.AI to see the wider incident cluster.

queries.label: Multi-hop: bridge two victims
queries.description: Shortest path linking the two separate Character.AI victims through the graph — the kind of multi-hop reasoning a chunk search cannot do.

queries.label: Most connected entities (hubs)
queries.description: Highest-degree entities — what the graph considers central to the corpus.

queries.label: Top community reports
queries.description: GraphRAG community summaries ranked by importance — the basis for global/abstract questions.
queries.cypher:
MATCH (c:Community)
WHERE c.summary <> ''
RETURN c.title, c.level, c.rank, left(c.summary, 240) AS summary
ORDER BY c.rank DESC LIMIT 10;
